sentences.text: From July 1, 2026, new graduate students in the US can no longer borrow federal Grad PLUS loans.
sentences.spoken: From July first, twenty twenty-six, new graduate students in the U.S. can no longer borrow federal Grad PLUS loans.

sentences.text: Leah, an illustrative student weeks from her first spring term, has two private offers on her laptop: 9% fixed, or variable starting lower, at 7.5%.
sentences.spoken: Leah, an illustrative student weeks from her first spring term, has two private offers on her laptop: nine percent fixed, or variable starting lower, at seven point five percent.

sentences.text: How much lower does a variable rate have to start before that risk has been worth it?
sentences.spoken: How much lower does a variable rate have to start before that risk has been worth it?

sentences.text: Students already enrolled and borrowing before July 2026 keep Grad PLUS for up to 3 more academic years, or for the time left in their program if that is shorter.
sentences.spoken: Students already enrolled and borrowing before July twenty twenty-six keep Grad PLUS for up to three more academic years, or for the time left in their program if that is shorter.

sentences.text: New students like Leah still have the basic federal loan, a Direct Unsubsidized loan, up to $20,500 a year and $100,000 total, with higher limits in professional programs like medicine or law.
sentences.spoken: New students like Leah still have the basic federal loan, a Direct Unsubsidized loan, up to twenty thousand five hundred dollars a year and one hundred thousand dollars total, with higher limits in professional programs like medicine or law.

sentences.text: When a program costs more than that after other aid, the rest can come from a private lender, and that's where Leah's two offers come from.
sentences.spoken: When a program costs more than that after other aid, the rest can come from a private lender, and that's where Leah's two offers come from.

sentences.text: Same lender, same amount, two kinds of rate.
sentences.spoken: Same lender, same amount, two kinds of rate.

sentences.text: Both are for $50,000 over 10 years, illustrative numbers, not a real lender's offer.
sentences.spoken: Both are for fifty thousand dollars over ten years, illustrative numbers, not a real lender's offer.

sentences.text: The variable loan's first payment is $593.51, about $40 less a month than the fixed $633.38.
sentences.spoken: The variable loan's first payment is five hundred ninety-three dollars and fifty-one cents, about forty dollars less a month than the fixed six hundred thirty-three dollars and thirty-eight cents.

sentences.text: A fixed rate never changes, so neither does the payment.
sentences.spoken: A fixed rate never changes, so neither does the payment.

sentences.text: A variable rate follows a market interest rate, so the rate and the payment rise and fall with it, and nobody knows where it goes next.
sentences.spoken: A variable rate follows a market interest rate, so the rate and the payment rise and fall with it, and nobody knows where it goes next.

sentences.text: The head start is the fixed rate minus the variable rate's starting rate; it is negative when the variable rate starts higher.
sentences.spoken: The head start is the fixed rate minus the variable rate's starting rate; it is negative when the variable rate starts higher.

sentences.text: Leah's fixed rate is 9% and her variable rate starts at 7.5%, so her head start is 1.5 points.
sentences.spoken: Leah's fixed rate is nine percent and her variable rate starts at seven point five percent, so her head start is one point five points.

sentences.text: A point here means one percentage point of interest.
sentences.spoken: A point here means one percentage point of interest.

sentences.text: Real offers differ, so a head start can be bigger, smaller, zero, or negative.
sentences.spoken: Real offers differ, so a head start can be bigger, smaller, zero, or negative.

sentences.text: This video replays Leah's illustrative loan through every 10-year stretch of US interest rates since January 1954.
sentences.spoken: This video replays Leah's illustrative loan through every ten-year stretch of U.S. interest rates since January nineteen fifty-four.

sentences.text: Each replay moves her rate up and down exactly as much as the 3-month Treasury bill rate moved in that stretch of history, and the data is US only.
sentences.spoken: Each replay moves her rate up and down exactly as much as the three-month Treasury bill rate moved in that stretch of history, and the data is U.S. only.

sentences.text: "Worth it" gets one plain meaning here: how often the variable loan cost more in total interest than the 9% fixed loan, and how much more at worst.
sentences.spoken: "Worth it" gets one plain meaning here: how often the variable loan cost more in total interest than the nine percent fixed loan, and how much more at worst.

sentences.text: Then the replay moves the head start, from 3 points down to a variable rate starting 1 point above the fixed one, to see where that history changes.
sentences.spoken: Then the replay moves the head start, from three points down to a variable rate starting one point above the fixed one, to see where that history changes.

sentences.text: By the end there's a line that any real offer can be held up against, including yours.
sentences.spoken: By the end there's a line that any real offer can be held up against, including yours.

sentences.text: This is history, not a forecast.
sentences.spoken: This is history, not a forecast.

sentences.text: And the first result looks like a contradiction.
sentences.spoken: And the first result looks like a contradiction.

sentences.text: Leah's variable rate rose above 9% at some point in 76.2% of stretches, about 3 in 4.
sentences.spoken: Leah's variable rate rose above nine percent at some point in seventy-six point two percent of stretches, about three in four.

sentences.text: Yet it cost more in total interest in 14.2%, about 1 in 7.
sentences.spoken: Yet it cost more in total interest in fourteen point two percent, about one in seven.

sentences.text: That 1 in 7 is made of two very different parts: 28.4%, more than 1 in 4, for starts from 1954 to 1980, and 3.5%, about 1 in 30, from 1981 on; the worst stretch, from April 1977, cost $11,219 more.
sentences.spoken: That one in seven is made of two very different parts: twenty-eight point four percent, more than one in four, for starts from nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty, and three point five percent, about one in thirty, from nineteen eighty-one on; the worst stretch, from April nineteen seventy-seven, cost eleven thousand two hundred nineteen dollars more.

sentences.text: The reason both are true is the head start.
sentences.spoken: The reason both are true is the head start.

sentences.text: Every month the variable rate sits below 9%, Leah pays less interest than on the fixed loan, and that saving builds a cushion.
sentences.spoken: Every month the variable rate sits below nine percent, Leah pays less interest than on the fixed loan, and that saving builds a cushion.

sentences.text: The cushion grows fastest at the start, when she owes the most, so every point of rate is charged on the biggest balance.
sentences.spoken: The cushion grows fastest at the start, when she owes the most, so every point of rate is charged on the biggest balance.

sentences.text: When the rate later climbs above 9%, the extra interest has to use up that cushion before the variable loan has cost more overall.
sentences.spoken: When the rate later climbs above nine percent, the extra interest has to use up that cushion before the variable loan has cost more overall.

sentences.text: A short jump above 9% only dents it; emptying it needs rates that rise early and stay high for years.
sentences.spoken: A short jump above nine percent only dents it; emptying it needs rates that rise early and stay high for years.

sentences.text: In a stretch where rates drift down, the cushion just keeps growing.
sentences.spoken: In a stretch where rates drift down, the cushion just keeps growing.

sentences.text: And the two halves of the record are very different.
sentences.spoken: And the two halves of the record are very different.

sentences.text: From 1954 to 1980, the Treasury bill rate mostly climbed, in waves.
sentences.spoken: From nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty, the Treasury bill rate mostly climbed, in waves.

sentences.text: It peaked at 16.3% in May 1981, then mostly drifted down over the following decades, with big swings.
sentences.spoken: It peaked at sixteen point three percent in May nineteen eighty-one, then mostly drifted down over the following decades, with big swings.

sentences.text: Same loan, same head start; the only difference is where in history it began.
sentences.spoken: Same loan, same head start; the only difference is where in history it began.

sentences.text: Loans started in the climbing years often met rates that rose early and stayed high, and loans started after the peak mostly rode rates down.
sentences.spoken: Loans started in the climbing years often met rates that rose early and stayed high, and loans started after the peak mostly rode rates down.

sentences.text: The best stretch began in August 1981, near that peak, and cost $15,295 less than the fixed loan.
sentences.spoken: The best stretch began in August nineteen eighty-one, near that peak, and cost fifteen thousand two hundred ninety-five dollars less than the fixed loan.

sentences.text: It belongs to the falling half, while the worst, April 1977, belongs to the climbing half, where far more of Leah's stretches cost more.
sentences.spoken: It belongs to the falling half, while the worst, April nineteen seventy-seven, belongs to the climbing half, where far more of Leah's stretches cost more.

sentences.text: Here is Leah's same loan, started in April 1977.
sentences.spoken: Here is Leah's same loan, started in April nineteen seventy-seven.

sentences.text: It begins at 7.5%, like every replay, and for a while her cushion grows.
sentences.spoken: It begins at seven point five percent, like every replay, and for a while her cushion grows.

sentences.text: Then the Treasury bill rate climbs year after year, and her rate follows it, to 19.3% at its highest.
sentences.spoken: Then the Treasury bill rate climbs year after year, and her rate follows it, to nineteen point three percent at its highest.

sentences.text: The cushion from her first months is soon gone, and every further month above 9% adds to what she owes in interest.
sentences.spoken: The cushion from her first months is soon gone, and every further month above nine percent adds to what she owes in interest.

sentences.text: Her payment reaches $863.36 a month, against the fixed $633.38.
sentences.spoken: Her payment reaches eight hundred sixty-three dollars and thirty-six cents a month, against the fixed six hundred thirty-three dollars and thirty-eight cents.

sentences.text: Over 10 years, the fixed loan charges $26,005 in interest, in dollars of the day.
sentences.spoken: Over ten years, the fixed loan charges twenty-six thousand five dollars in interest, in dollars of the day.

sentences.text: Leah's variable loan charges 43% more interest than the fixed loan, the worst stretch in the whole replay.
sentences.spoken: Leah's variable loan charges forty-three percent more interest than the fixed loan, the worst stretch in the whole replay.

sentences.text: This replay has no rate cap; a real loan's cap, if low enough, would have made this worst case smaller.
sentences.spoken: This replay has no rate cap; a real loan's cap, if low enough, would have made this worst case smaller.

sentences.text: So far, every result has been for one pair of rates, 7.5% against 9%.
sentences.spoken: So far, every result has been for one pair of rates, seven point five percent against nine percent.

sentences.text: So the replay ran again, holding the fixed rate at 9% and moving only where the variable rate starts.
sentences.spoken: So the replay ran again, holding the fixed rate at nine percent and moving only where the variable rate starts.

sentences.text: Each starting point is a different offer someone could be holding.
sentences.spoken: Each starting point is a different offer someone could be holding.

sentences.text: Leah's 1.5 points gives the split already heard, with her April 1977 worst.
sentences.spoken: Leah's one point five points gives the split already heard, with her April nineteen seventy-seven worst.

sentences.text: At 2 points, none of the starts from 1981 on cost more, but 20.4% of the starts from 1954 to 1980 still did, the worst by $9,472.
sentences.spoken: At two points, none of the starts from nineteen eighty-one on cost more, but twenty point four percent of the starts from nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty still did, the worst by nine thousand four hundred seventy-two dollars.

sentences.text: At 3 points, still none from 1981 on, but 10.5% of the starts from 1954 to 1980 cost more, the worst by $6,033.
sentences.spoken: At three points, still none from nineteen eighty-one on, but ten point five percent of the starts from nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty cost more, the worst by six thousand thirty-three dollars.

sentences.text: With a smaller head start, or a variable rate that starts higher, more stretches cost more in both halves, and the worst gets bigger.
sentences.spoken: With a smaller head start, or a variable rate that starts higher, more stretches cost more in both halves, and the worst gets bigger.

sentences.text: At every head start tested, the worst stretch began in April 1977.
sentences.spoken: At every head start tested, the worst stretch began in April nineteen seventy-seven.

sentences.text: And at every head start tested, some of the starts from 1954 to 1980 still cost more.
sentences.spoken: And at every head start tested, some of the starts from nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty still cost more.

sentences.text: So, back to the question: how much lower does a variable rate have to start before the risk has been worth it?
sentences.spoken: So, back to the question: how much lower does a variable rate have to start before the risk has been worth it?

sentences.text: Measured as how often it cost more in total interest than the 9% fixed loan, and how much more at worst, history gives two answers.
sentences.spoken: Measured as how often it cost more in total interest than the nine percent fixed loan, and how much more at worst, history gives two answers.

sentences.text: From 1981 on, a 2-point head start was enough every time; from 1954 to 1980, even 3 points was not, and the worst still cost $6,033 more.
sentences.spoken: From nineteen eighty-one on, a two point head start was enough every time; from nineteen fifty-four to nineteen eighty, even three points was not, and the worst still cost six thousand thirty-three dollars more.

sentences.text: Which kind of history comes next is something no replay can show.
sentences.spoken: Which kind of history comes next is something no replay can show.
